For \(n\ge 2\),
\[
a_n=S_n-S_{n-1},
\]
and \(S_n,S_{n-1}\in\{1,3\}\). Thus
\[
a_n\in\{1-1,\,3-3,\,3-1,\,1-3\}=\{0,2,-2\}.
\]
So only \(a_1=S_1\) can be \(1\) or \(3\), but not both. Hence the distinct terms can be at most
\[
\{1,0,2,-2\}
\]
if \(S_1=1\), or \(\{3,0,2,-2\}\) if \(S_1=3\).

This bound is achievable, e.g.
\[
a_1=1,\quad a_2=0,\quad a_3=2,\quad a_4=-2,\quad a_n=0\ (n\ge5),
\]
whose partial sums are \(1,1,3,1,1,\ldots\in\{1,3\}\).

Therefore the maximum value of \(k\) is
\[
\boxed{4}.
\]
